review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–62), which has two theorems. nat_progression_population_card_le is a min-element argument: erase the minimum, embed the rest in a filtered Ioc, and apply integer_interval_residue_error. nat_residue_population_card_le splits S by residue class and sums the fiber bound over the image. The two proofs share no repeated reasoning.

I also searched the Ostmann directory for the same fiber-sum step: card_eq_sum_card_image followed by sum_le_sum. It appears in KernelDiscardBound.lean (~l.48–52), KernelPopulationDiscard.lean (~l.67–70) and DensityZeroBins.lean (~l.91–96). The first of these is real-valued, as the target is. The second is ℕ-valued, where Mathlib's Finset.card_le_mul_card_image already covers the same fiber-sum step. In each case the step is a 2–4 line calculation (sum_le_sum and a constant sum). That is too short to meet the rubric's threshold of nontrivial repeated machinery, and a shared real-valued helper would be little more than a thin wrapper. The residue-error step in the target is also used once; the other uses of integer_interval_residue_error (DivisibleResidueCount, PeriodicResidueSum) have different surrounding arguments. I found no justified finding. I did not check the other Ostmann files in full.
